property_summary: For any deployed C, calling currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion() after applying the product's payoff transform (i.e. transformed.price equals payoffDefinition().transform(original.price)); the mutant that returns the raw oracle.currentVersion() without _transform will sometimes return a different price for some oracle price inputs.

For any oracle price input, C.currentVersion() always returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoffDefinition transform applied to the underlying oracle.currentVersion().price; the mutant that returns the raw oracle.currentVersion() (omitting the transform) will for some oracle prices produce a different price and thus violate this rule.

For any oracle version returned by the oracle, C.currentVersion() must return the oracle version with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (i.e. transformed.price == payoffDefinition().transform(oraclePrice)); the mutant that omits _transform will sometimes return a different price and thus violate this property.

For every oracle-reported price, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle version whose price has been transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant returns the raw oracle price (no transform) and thus for some oracle prices the returned price differs.

For every oracle-reported currentVersion, C.currentVersion() returns the same OracleVersion but with price equal to payoffDefinition().transform(oracle.currentVersion().price); the mutant omits the transform and thus for some oracle price inputs the returned price differs.

For any oracle state, calling currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion with exactly one application of the product's _transform; the mutant double-applies _transform so for some oracle prices (non-zero) the returned price differs between correct and mutant.

For any oracle-returned price p, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle version with price transformed exactly once by payoffDefinition.transform; the mutant double-transforms the price so for some oracle prices (non-zero) the returned price differs.

For every oracle price input, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's current version with the product's payoff transformation applied exactly once; the mutant sometimes applies the transformation twice and thus returns a different transformed price for some oracle-returned prices.

For any oracle currentVersion returned price, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle version with the product's payoff transformation applied exactly once; the mutant sometimes applies the transform twice and thus returns a different price for some oracle outputs.

For any oracle current version returned price, C.currentVersion() returns that oracle version with the product payoff transform applied exactly once (so calling currentVersion() on the correct contract yields a result equal to applying _transform once to the oracle output); the mutant double-applies _transform and therefore for some oracle-returned prices the returned price differs, so equality with a single-application transform is violated.

For any oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) always returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the product's payoffDefinition.transform applied to the underlying oracle().atVersion(id).price; the mutant returns the untransformed price for some ids, violating this rule.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals payoffDefinition().transform( oracle().atVersion(id).price ); the mutant returns the raw oracle price for some ids, so the transformed price equality can be violated.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals payoffDefinition().transform( oracle().atVersion(id).price ); the mutant returns the raw oracle price for some ids, so this equality is violated.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals payoffDefinition().transform applied to the underlying oracle().atVersion(id).price; the mutant returns the raw underlying price (omitting transform) for some oracleVersion ids, so the equality can be violated.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals payoffDefinition().transform( oracle().atVersion(id).price ); the mutant omits the transform and thus for some oracle versions the returned price differs.

For any stored funding fee value in the contract, the reference implementation returns exactly that stored funding fee when calling fundingFee(); the mutant that doubles the stored value will sometimes return a different (larger) value, so there exists inputs where fundingFee() differs between reference and mutant.

For any stored funding fee value, calling fundingFee() returns exactly the stored funding fee (reference); the mutant that returns twice the stored funding fee will produce a different returned value for some stored funding fee inputs (i.e. whenever stored funding fee != 0).
For any stored funding fee value, calling fundingFee() returns that stored value; the mutant that returns the stored value doubled will differ whenever the stored funding fee is non-zero.

For all stored fundingFee values, calling fundingFee() returns the stored value (not doubled); the mutant that returns twice the stored funding fee will violate this when the stored funding fee is non-zero.

For any stored funding fee value, the correct contract's fundingFee() returns exactly the stored _fundingFee (i.e. calling fundingFee() yields the stored value); the mutant that doubles the stored value will return a different value whenever the stored funding fee is non-zero.

For every input the reference contract returns the stored taker fee unchanged from storage (i.e. takerFee() == stored value); the mutant multiplies the stored taker fee by 2, so there exist inputs where takerFee() != the stored value (detectable when stored value != 0).

For every stored taker fee value in the product, calling takerFee() returns exactly that stored value; the mutant multiplies the stored taker fee by 2 so when the stored value is non-zero takerFee() will differ (the test fuzzes a stored value and checks equality between a setter-observed stored value and takerFee()).
